title: OpenStream — your phone is now an OBS camera
description: OpenStream — turn an Android phone into a native OBS camera over local Wi-Fi. every lens, up to 1080p60, AAC audio, live camera controls, zero cloud.

sections.heading: Every lens
sections.text: (03) Features 01 Every lens Ultra-wide, main, telephoto and front. Switch on the phone or from OBS. → 02 Control from OBS A Camera Control dock inside OBS for lens, zoom and torch. Hands off the phone. → 03 Finds your PC OBS computers on your network appear in the app. Tap one. No IP addresses. → 04 Reconnects itself Brief Wi-Fi drops recover on their own. The source stays put in your scene. → 05 Real audio AAC audio from the phone mic, synced with the video and on its own track. → 06 Local only No accounts, no relay, no telemetry. Video never leaves your network. →

sections.text: (05) Install Android Phone Windows OBS Linux OBS Needs: Windows 10/11 x64 · OBS Studio 30+ OBS plugin installer .exe — Recommended — finds OBS for you ↓ Manual ZIP .zip — For custom OBS install paths ↓ Using the ZIP? Extract everything, then right-click install-openstream-plugin.bat → Run as administrator. All files & release notes ↗ 1 Close OBS The plugin can't be replaced while OBS has it loaded. 2 Run the installer It asks for admin rights once and installs into your OBS folder. 3 Reopen OBS The OpenStream source and Camera Control dock are ready.

sections.heading: FIVE MOVES. THEN YOU'RE ON.
sections.text: (06) Go live FIVE MOVES. THEN YOU'RE ON. 1 Same network Phone and computer on the same Wi-Fi. 5 GHz or Wi-Fi 6 if you have it. 2 Add the source In OBS: Sources → + → OpenStream. One source per phone. 3 Pick your computer Open the app — your PC appears under “Choose your OBS computer”. Tap it. 4 Frame the shot Choose a lens and quality. Turn on Stay to keep the screen awake. 5 Go live Stream or record as usual. Fine-tune from the Camera Control dock.
